commands.guidance: Use fetch for unrendered HTML, images or files; document for browser-rendered DOM; open/observe for UI. --save writes the complete body; stdout and --output contain dw.resource.v1 metadata and body_file only. Existing save files are replaced only after successful acquisition and network cleanup. Save and metadata paths must differ. Default system route; direct is explicit, with no automatic route or tool fallback. Delivery commits in order: body rename, optional metadata file, then stdout. Each committed output remains if a later delivery fails. Encoding or metadata-write failures exit 2 and, when stdout works, report diagnostics preserving byte counts without body_file. A stdout failure returns exit 2 and stderr; an already committed metadata file may still contain successful body_file metadata. Inspect available committed metadata or settle budgets conservatively. Consumers verify MIME/signature and meaning: an HTTP 200 challenge page is not an image or accepted article. DNS resolver choice is per call: system by default, or an explicit public numeric-IP HTTPS /dns-query endpoint. Only use that endpoint when the caller explicitly chooses a public DNS strategy; never switch after a timeout. No resolver fallback, environment override or cross-call cache. Resolver DNS traffic shares the acquisition network-byte budget. A third-party resolver learns queried hostnames and the client/proxy source IP, not the original URL path or response content; existing proxy trust remains. TLS must validate its IP SAN.
commands.summary: Save a complete public HTTP response body without JavaScript or a browser

commands.usage: observe --id NAME [--screenshot PATH] [--content text|list|table] [--health] [--tree] [--top N] [--budget B] [--all] [--annotate] [--hit-audit]
commands.guidance: The perception verb: returns the thin default {elements@rN, user_state, run_id, step}; additive flags are freely combined. --screenshot writes the actual PNG and returns its path — read the real PNG before visual actions. Channel states distinguish captured/unavailable/not-requested; an unavailable channel cannot prove zero errors. @rN refs share one space with act: `act "click @r3"` resolves the refs this observe just returned. --all is a census without operable refs. Reobserve after an action, resize, tab switch, navigation or intervention before using any ref or screenshot coordinate. --annotate draws the browser-chrome occlusion evidence outline (mobile persona debugging), not content annotation — for annotated content crops use excerpt.

arguments.description: JSON array; each entry becomes one cropped PNG screenshot: {name, targets:[...], highlight:[phrases], box_style:{color:"#rrggbb", width:int(css px)}, highlight_color:"#rrggbb", crop_margin:int(css px)}. targets resolve elements on the open page: "id:ELEMID" by DOM id (dots allowed, no CSS escaping needed), "title:ELEMID" for the .ltx_title inside that id (arXiv headings), or a bare value as a CSS selector. highlight phrases are matched inside the target text with whitespace tolerance, skipping MathML annotations and spanning inline links/emphasis; each match is painted with a translucent highlighter and every matched line keeps readable text.

examples: dw-browser excerpt --id paper --spec '[{"name":"readout","targets":["id:S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1"],"highlight":["Instant readouts have approximately 2–8% higher latency"]}]'
commands.guidance: Screenshot verb (read-only observation class): crops page regions as PNG images with a red box around the target union and translucent highlights over chosen phrases — built for quoting web originals (papers, docs) into markdown. It never mutates the page, needs no write grant or allow-host, and does not invalidate observation refs (a 20-image batch needs no re-observe). One full-page capture serves the whole spec. Unresolved targets and unmatched phrases are explicit per-entry business results in missing (exit stays 0); entries whose targets all miss produce no file. warnings reports fixed/sticky elements overlapping the box and images still loading. Elements taller than the viewport are captured whole. Style defaults: red 3px box, #ffe94d highlight, 14px crop margin; override per entry with box_style/highlight_color/crop_margin.
commands.summary: Crop read-only annotated PNG screenshot excerpts from the open page

commands.usage: act click [TARGET] --id NAME [verb flags — see flags below]
commands.guidance: Typed interaction verb through the shared action contract. A TARGET is a returned opaque `@...` ref from the latest observe, an explicit `css=...`/`role=...` locator, or coordinates with --x/--y (plus --unit css-px --frame viewport --observation-id CAPTURE for coordinates). Observe first, act, then reobserve: refs are bound to one observation and die on navigation/tab switch/resize. Literal text is never an action string. Unknown or partially dispatched acts require observation before retry. Clicks the target center (respects occlusion: a click blocked by browser chrome fails loud).
commands.summary: Click a visible target; count 2 or button right selects its mouse variant
